notes: Changed rule, graded against the current text: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes only the SKILL.md table row for ex_unit.md and renames testing.md to ex_unit.md in the committed part (3e3581d..7fef5b5); the uncommitted part (git diff 7fef5b5) rewrites this rule's prose, adds the Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, rewords the do: rule's mixing sentence and Before you finish step 1. Only the first is on this case's list. The sentences that now decide the verdict are "When a call's result is passed on, matched against or nested in another call, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name that says what it is, one field per line, with a blank line between multi-line statements." and "A call whose result is itself bound to a name may take its options inline, as `formatter` does below". Violating runs: 1 of 4 (haiku-1); 2026-10-22-c had 1 of 5 (sonnet-2), check-7 0 of 4, check-6 3 of 4.

How the one in-scope literal was read. Haiku-1's :ets.new(name, [ / :named_table, / :public, / :ordered_set, / read_concurrency: true, / write_concurrency: true / ]) (lines 93-99) is a statement whose result is discarded: not bound to a name, not passed on, not matched, not nested. The bound-result permission does not cover it, the title ("Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call") and the unchanged Use ETS example in processes.md (table_options = [...] then a bare :ets.new(name, table_options)) both name such a list, and 2026-10-22-c counted exactly this shape (sonnet-2's discarded :ets.new with a six-line list) as violated, so it is graded violated here. Wording gap: the new first sentence lists only passed on, matched against or nested, so a reader who takes it as the rule's whole scope finds a discarded-result call in neither group and would call haiku-1 not covered. If discarded-result calls are meant to be named, the prose should say so, for example by scoping the rule to every call except one whose result is bound to a name. Joined, haiku-1's call is 106 characters, so the list would span several lines whatever the author did; the first Write already had this shape and mix format changed nothing.

Every map, struct or keyword literal spanning several lines inside a call, per run. Haiku-1: one, the :ets.new/2 options above (lines 93-99), result discarded, not named first. Haiku-2: none; its :ets.new/2 options are one-line literals (lines 109, 110, both discarded), GenServer.start_link/3 at line 79 is one line and passed on as start_link/1's result. Its :ets.select_count(@requests_table, [ / {{{user_key, :"$1", :_}}, [{:>, :"$1", cutoff}], [true]} / ]) (lines 131-133) is passed on as count_in_window/2's result and was broken by the author (joined, exactly 98 characters), but it is a match spec, a list of one tuple, not a map, struct or keyword list, so it is not counted. Sonnet-1: none; its :ets.new/2 options are one-line literals (lines 130, 131, discarded), Keyword.validate!(opts, [:limits_file, :name, default_limit: @default_limit]) at line 87 is one line and bound to opts, and its match specs are named on one line (match_spec, lines 171 and 177). Sonnet-2: one, built first: table_options = [ / :named_table, / :public, / :ordered_set, / read_concurrency: true, / write_concurrency: true / ] (lines 129-135), blank lines 128 and 136, then :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 137, discarded), the processes.md example with :ordered_set, so clean. Not counted: sonnet-2's raise ArgumentError, / "rate limit for ... got: #{inspect(limit)}" (lines 179-180), a string the formatter wrapped; the moduledoc child lists, all bound to children (haiku-1 lines 15-17, haiku-2 lines 27-31, sonnet-1 lines 26-30, sonnet-2 lines 26-30); sonnet-2's moduledoc map (lines 9-12), which is the limits file's content, not a call argument. Against 2026-10-22-c the tiers swap: there haiku wrote one-line options and sonnet-2 the inline list; here sonnet-2 names table_options and haiku-1 writes the inline list after reading SKILL.md and processes.md.

The other nine rules have unchanged text since 3e3581d and are graded to the standard of 2026-10-22-c/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json: an if on one boolean condition is clean; a single fallible call handled with a case whose success clause returns the next step's result is clean under the with rule (sonnet-1 read_limits/1 lines 145-150, as haiku-2 there); a run with no with and no fallible {:ok, _} | {:error, _} call is not exercised (haiku-1 read_limits!/1 and haiku-2 load_limits!/1 raise through File.read! and JSON/Jason.decode!, sonnet-2 load_limits!/1 through Code.eval_file/1); key, row_key, request and similar local names are not counted under Naming; a start_link/1 with no :name option and fixed table names violates the responsive rule (haiku-2, as haiku-2 there); reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict. One call made fresh for this batch: sonnet-1's @doc for check/2 has an ## Examples section (lines 100-106) written as MyApp.RateLimiter.check(42) / #=> :ok / MyApp.RateLimiter.check(42) / #=> {:error, :rate_limited}, which has no iex> prompt and so cannot run as a doctest, and whose second result is wrong at the default limit of 60; the Comments rule says "Include `## Examples` that work as doctests", and 2026-10-22-b counted a failing doctest under that rule, so Comments is violated for sonnet-1. Runs with no ## Examples are not counted, as before.

Designs. All four keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer, and the caller inserts its row, counts with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes its row when over the limit, with a handle_info/2 sweep (haiku-1 every minute, haiku-2 every 10 s keeping two windows, sonnet-1 every 30 s, sonnet-2 every minute), so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS, Keep each process behind one module and the call/cast and per-key cleanup parts of the responsive rule are clean in all four. Limits live as rows in the same table (haiku-1), in a second table (haiku-2, sonnet-1) or in :persistent_term (sonnet-2). Every run reads the limits file inside init/1: haiku-1 line 91 (File.read! at line 132), haiku-2 line 111 (File.read! at line 144), sonnet-1 line 128 (:file.consult/1 at line 146), sonnet-2 line 126 (Code.eval_file/1 at line 166). Sonnet-1 takes the default limit from the :default_limit start option, not the file. Callers are shown only in the moduledocs.

Verification, in scratch copies under grading11/rate-limiter-skill. All four pass mix format --check-formatted; the only line over 98 characters is haiku-1 line 57, inside a @doc string. All four compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.4, OTP 29); haiku-2 prints one warning that Jason.decode!/1 is undefined (line 145) because Jason is not installed; it is a Phoenix dependency, and haiku-2's own test shimmed it, so it is not counted, as 2026-10-22-c did not count opus-1's missing Plug. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5 (haiku-2 with a Jason shim over :json); where :name is accepted (all but haiku-2) a second instance under name: :other kept its own count (2 of 50); haiku-2's second start_link/1 returned {:error, {:already_started, _}}; an injected expired row was removed by one :sweep message and the other rows kept. The first Write of each session equals its final file, and each session ran mix format right after it.

All four runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier, head 7fef5b5 with uncommitted true, and skill_hash f7ec139c0d805a00f972075a62230bdba96c0ae318390191b74a4547827c106c, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/. Reads: all four read SKILL.md, processes.md and ecto-phoenix.md (haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 with three Read calls; sonnet-2 read SKILL.md and cat the two references in one command). Expected reads (processes.md) is met in all four. No opus run in this check batch, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule.
